name: 01-operations-overview
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a single exceptionally polished high-fidelity desktop software concept screenshot, landscape 16:9, ideally 2560x1440 or larger. Product is AIRPORT RECOVERY LIVE, an AI airport disruption simulator. Art direction inspired by the precision and restraint of Palantir-style geospatial operations software, with an original identity and no Palantir logo. This must feel like expensive, real enterprise software designed by a superb product design team. Edge-to-edge app interface, no laptop, no monitor bezel, no room, no poster. Extremely crisp typography, clean alignment, consistent 8-pixel spacing, fine 1-pixel dividers, restrained small radius corners. Graphite/navy panels, near-black map canvas, off-white primary text, muted steel secondary text. Thin cyan for tracked aircraft, amber for incidents and proposed changes, mint for validated alternatives, red only for unavailable resources. Realistic detailed 3D geospatial terrain, desaturated satellite-like land textures, roads, airport terminal, apron and runway, with subtle dimensional lighting. Ground should be believable inland southern Romania, not a coastal fantasy airport. Maps and telemetry are illustrative, not verified real geography. Make the map occupy about 70 percent of the screen; concise narrow left resource rail, a carefully composed right decision inspector, compact top bar, thin bottom time ruler and a beautiful small voice waveform/command strip. Keep overlay labels carefully separated and anchored to objects. Readable useful information, no walls of gibberish, no oversized KPI cards, no donut charts, no neon cyberpunk glow, no holographic gadgets, no military weapons. Use these exact consistent chrome labels: 'RECOVERY LIVE', 'CRAIOVA OPERATIONS', 'SIMULATION', 'RESOURCES', 'DECISION LOG'. Persistent small footer: 'CONCEPT • ILLUSTRATIVE DATA'. Aircraft are elegant realistic miniatures at geographically plausible positions, not giant toy jets. This is concept art for an unbuilt product. No fabricated latency or performance claims. Render only the few specified labels clearly and use restrained abstract short rows where additional UI density is needed.
SCENE 1 — OPERATIONS OVERVIEW. A calm and commanding bird's-eye oblique view over the entire airport, one runway and a beautifully detailed glass terminal with a few aircraft on the apron, two inbound aircraft with delicate altitude trails. The geography is the hero. Subtle illuminated gate markers G01, G02, G03; small buses on roads outside the terminal. Left rail lists 'CRA / Craiova', 'OTP / Bucharest', 'SBZ / Sibiu', then short flight and ground resource lists. Right inspector header 'NETWORK STATUS', with three refined rows 'Flights tracked 05', 'Transfer vehicles 06', 'Active incidents 00'. Beneath it a small empty 'DECISION LOG' state 'Waiting for an event'. Bottom voice strip has a refined waveform and 'Describe a scenario'. Tiny map legend separates 'Observed traffic' from 'Simulated resources'. Show a tasteful selection outline around the Craiova airport footprint. Camera is low enough to perceive terminal architecture but high enough to read the whole airport. Elegant hierarchy, subtle atmospheric depth, astonishingly polished and plausible product screenshot.

SCENE 2 — BUS BREAKDOWN AND LIVE RECOVERY. Same product and exact visual language. Map zooms to the landside airport roads and transfer staging area, detailed terminal visible in the upper left. A selected failed bus B12 has an amber incident pin and a halted route segment. Two replacement buses B04 and B07 have mint proposed routes drawn as thin precise dashed polylines on the roads towards passenger pickup points. Small grouped passenger markers remain together. The visual tells a clear cause-and-effect story: one failed resource, affected passengers, new allocation. Left resource list shows 'B12 / Unavailable', 'B04 / 16 seats', 'B07 / 12 seats'. Right inspector title 'TRANSFER DISRUPTION', exact concise text '28 passengers affected', 'B04 + B07', 'Capacity verified', 'Plan proposed'. A compact comparison has two understated option rows with the selected alternative lightly mint tinted, not loud cards. Bottom voice command strip displays the exact Romanian sentence: 'Autocarul B12 s-a defectat.' A second small line reads 'Replanning affected itineraries'. A fine event timeline has 'Incident', 'Evaluate', 'Validate', 'Propose', with Propose active. Original route amber and replacement paths mint; aircraft context cyan. Professional geospatial operational analysis, emotionally legible at a glance, realistic satellite terrain and architecture, immaculate typography and spacing. No claim of measured milliseconds.

SCENE 3 — AIRCRAFT DIVERSION WITH NETWORK CASCADE. Same product and visual design system, camera pulls back to a sophisticated regional oblique 3D map of southern Romania: Craiova to the west, Bucharest to the east, Sibiu to the north, subtle Carpathian terrain farther north. This is illustrative geography, not a surveyed map. Three clearly labeled airport nodes 'CRA', 'OTP', 'SBZ'. A selected inbound passenger jet has a thin cyan observed track; its original proposed approach to CRA is faded amber and ends at an unavailable-airport marker. A new mint scenario trajectory curves toward OTP with subtle altitude cues. Ground transfer corridors from OTP back toward CRA and hotel nodes reveal downstream effects, carefully subordinate to the air route. Right inspector title 'DIVERSION SCENARIO', with 'CRA unavailable', 'Alternatives: OTP / SBZ', 'Selected plan: OTP', and three clean consequence rows 'Ground transfers', 'Hotel capacity', 'Passenger connections'. A clear amber banner on the map says 'SIMULATED DIVERSION'. Bottom voice strip displays exact Romanian: 'Avionul nu poate ateriza la Craiova.' Below, small English line 'Compare feasible recovery plans'. A narrow lower timeline shows cascading flight, bus and hotel changes as neat aligned bars, not a giant dashboard. The right decision log visibly contains 'Alternatives evaluated', 'Constraints checked', 'Recovery plan proposed'. Meaningful network complexity with restrained visual density, map still dominant and luminous objects grounded in realistic terrain. A production-quality enterprise command center, highly polished, no pretend ATC certification and no performance numbers.
